$comment: SP-HR-1 / CAP-068 / T-23 — the client-side outbound-host allowlist.
requestHosts is the one that matters: hosts the browser is permitted to talk
to. It is EMPTY, and adding an entry is an architecture decision recorded in
control/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md, not a code change. The prohibition on
client-side third-party hosts is unconditional (AGENTS.md). Server-side
subprocessors are a different question and are registered elsewhere.
vendorStringHosts is narrower than it looks. A minified third-party bundle
contains URLs that are TEXT, not destinations: XML namespace identifiers, a
documentation link inside an error message, a URL-parsing base. Entries here:
- apply ONLY to the built-bundle scan, never to apps/web/src;
- are IGNORED when the URL appears in a request-shaped context (fetch,
an allowlisted host that is actually being called still fails the build;
- are printed on every run, so they cannot accumulate unnoticed.
Each entry states which dependency puts the string there. If a dependency is
removed, its entry must go with it.

vendorStringHosts.reason: XML/SVG/MathML namespace identifiers emitted by react-dom (createElementNS). Namespace URIs are identifiers, never fetched.
react-dom production error decoder link, embedded as message text in invariant errors.
@tanstack/react-router migration-guidance link, embedded as message text in a development warning.
Attribution comment in the Tailwind preflight stylesheet. A CSS comment issues no request.
@tanstack/react-router uses 'http://localhost' as an inert base when parsing relative paths with the URL constructor.
